takeaway: Necrosis: groups of cells, swelling and lysis, loss of membrane integrity, inflammation. Apoptosis: single cells, shrinkage, intact membrane, no inflammation.

question.text: Which one of the following is characteristic of necrosis in comparison with apoptosis?
question.say: Which one of the following is characteristic of necrosis in comparison with apoptosis?

lines.text: Start with apoptosis, on the left. The cell packs its bag and quietly shrinks into small bubbles. Its membrane stays intact.
Neighbouring cells eat the bubbles tidily, and there is no inflammation. It involves single cells.
Necrosis is the opposite. The cell swells, its membrane is lost, and it bursts, with groups of cells collapsing together.
That brings in the neutrophil firefighters. Necrosis causes an inflammatory response.
So the membrane staying intact, shrinkage and single cells all describe apoptosis, and apoptosis is the physiological process.
The characteristic of necrosis is the inflammatory response.
